items.title: Denise Morel Interview, 1965-05-07
items.q: The first time I heard Armstrong with Barnaby Bigard, I was a bit upset because I found that he was making a commercial music.

ctx.x: Well, what do you think about the New Orleans musicians who have come there in person? Have you heard Bonnie Bigard, Albert Nicholas, any of those? Yes.

The first time I heard Armstrong with Barnaby Bigard, I was a bit upset because I found that he was making a commercial music. It had a bit of a fabric, a lack of spontaneity. And when I saw Joe Killington when he was in Paris, it was even worse. I thought it was terrible. It was all except jazz. And they were very surprised by the exigence of the French public They thought that the French were more exigent. They thought that the French were more exigent than the American.
